description: Cloud Village at DEF CON 27 covers cloud security for AWS, Azure, GCP, and other platforms. The 7 talks explore Azure assessment, cloud policy-as-code, security auditing with Splunk/ELK, automotive cloud hacking, secure defaults, air-gapping, and AWS security best practices.

talks.title: DYI Azure Security Assesment
talks.teaser: DIY methodology for assessing and auditing Azure cloud security posture.
talks.summary:
### Practical Security Auditing for Microsoft Azure
At 00:00, application security expert Tanya Janca delivers a practical, step-by-step guide to conducting comprehensive security assessments of Microsoft Azure cloud subscriptions without disrupting production services.

### Scoping and Stakeholder Communication
At 06:00, Janca highlights the operational etiquette of cloud auditing. Security assessors must establish transparent rules of engagement with internal system administrators to ensure audit activities do not trigger unintended service outages or operational alarm.

### Benchmarking with Azure Security Center and Policies
At 12:01, the speaker explores built-in governance tools. She demonstrates auditing Azure environments against the CIS Azure Foundations Benchmark using Azure Security Center, highlighting common oversights such as unencrypted storage blobs, exposed management endpoints, and unforced multi-factor authentication (MFA).

### Virtual Machine Hygiene and Disk Encryption
At 18:01, Janca examines compute security, auditing unattached virtual disks, checking OS image patch cadences, and verifying that virtual machine storage volumes are protected by Azure Key Vault-managed encryption keys.

### Network Security Groups and Perimeter Defense
Concluding between 24:02 and 30:04, Janca addresses perimeter network architecture. She demonstrates auditing Network Security Groups (NSGs) to close public RDP (port 3389) and SSH (port 22) exposures, and details configuring Web Application Firewall (WAF) policies on Azure Application Gateways to protect cloud services against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities.

talks.title: PacBot Policy as Code from T Mobile OSS
talks.teaser: Policy-as-code automation for managing cloud security and compliance policies.
talks.summary:
### Scaling Cloud Compliance with Policy as Code
At 00:00, Setu Parimi from T-Mobile introduces PacBot (Policy as Code Bot), an open-source platform designed for continuous cloud compliance monitoring and automated policy enforcement, at the Cloud Village.

### Enterprise Multi-Cloud Governance Architecture
At 05:08, Parimi details PacBot's distributed architectural framework. Designed to govern thousands of cloud accounts across AWS and Azure, PacBot utilizes serverless event collectors, auto-scaling microservices, and an administrative dashboard to track security posture in real time.

### Automated Asset Inventory and Shadow IT Discovery
At 10:13, the presentation examines the difficulty of maintaining complete cloud visibility. Parimi describes how PacBot correlates Shodan internet scans with internal asset catalogs to trace external-facing IP addresses, identify untracked shadow IT infrastructure, and assign ownership to cloud assets.

### Managing Policy Exceptions and Developer Workflows
At 14:54, the speaker reviews exception handling. PacBot incorporates structured exception workflows allowing developers to request temporary policy exemptions for testing or staged patching, ensuring security teams maintain compliance oversight without halting development velocity.

### Defining Policies as Code and Automated Remediation
Concluding between 19:51 and 26:37, Parimi walks through authoring policies in code. He demonstrates how custom rules flag unapproved IAM roles, open security groups, and unencrypted databases, triggering automated remediation actions to resolve non-compliant resources autonomously.

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, phishing techniques, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses in organizations.

talks.title: Your Blacklist is Dead: Airgap Everything
talks.teaser: Network segmentation and airgapping strategies for cloud infrastructure defense.
talks.summary:
### The Demise of Traditional IP and Domain Blacklisting
At 00:00, cybersecurity researcher Erick Galinkin delivers an incisive critique of perimeter security models, arguing that conventional domain and IP blacklists are fundamentally ineffective against modern threat actors.

### The Evolution of Cloud-Hosted Command and Control
At 05:01, Galinkin chronicles how adversaries have weaponized legitimate cloud infrastructure for over a decade, tracing command-and-control (C2) traffic from Zeus botnets on AWS EC2 in 2009 to modern malware abusing Google App Engine and cloud CDNs.

### Living Off Trusted Cloud Platforms
At 10:00, the speaker details how contemporary malware utilizes legitimate services—including GitHub, Pastebin, Discord, Slack, and Google Drive—for covert C2 communication. Because enterprise firewalls cannot blacklist these mission-critical domains, perimeter egress filters fail to intercept malicious traffic.

### The Triviality of In-Memory Payload Delivery
At 15:01, Galinkin demonstrates the simplicity of execution bypasses. A simple `curl` command piping raw scripts directly into runtime interpreters downloads and executes code without touching disk, easily evading signature-based network defenses.

### Airgapping Everything: Zero-Trust Enclaves
Concluding between 20:00 and 25:00, Galinkin urges organizations to abandon perimeter-based trust. Enterprise defense requires implementing software airgapping, default-deny outbound network filtering, and strict micro-segmentation so production cloud workloads cannot initiate arbitrary outbound internet connections.

talks.title: Using Pareto's Principle for Securing AWS with SCPs
talks.teaser: AWS Service Control Policies for efficient cloud security and compliance management.
talks.summary:
### Maximizing AWS Security Impact via Pareto's Principle
At 00:00, cloud security architect Ayman Elsawah presents on utilizing Pareto's Principle (the 80/20 rule) to achieve maximum defensive impact using AWS Service Control Policies (SCPs) at the Cloud Village. Elsawah discusses common barriers to SCP adoption.

### Overcoming Fear of Service Control Policies
At 05:48, Elsawah addresses why many enterprises hesitate to implement SCPs. Because SCPs define organization-wide permission boundaries that override individual IAM policies, administrators fear that minor configuration errors could disrupt production cloud workloads.

### Phased Testing and Staged Rollout Strategies
At 11:26, the speaker outlines a structured testing methodology. By establishing a dedicated hierarchy within AWS Organizations, administrators can test restrictive SCPs in sandbox and staging organizational units (OUs) before promoting policies into production accounts.

### High-Impact Preventative Guardrails
At 17:13, Elsawah showcases high-value SCP policies that yield maximum security benefit with minimal operational friction. He demonstrates policies that restrict unauthorized geographic regions, block modifications to logging services (CloudTrail and GuardDuty), and prevent disabling multi-factor authentication.

### Cloud Governance and Shadow IT Discovery
Concluding between 24:03 and 31:26, Elsawah reviews multi-account procurement strategies. He discusses techniques for identifying unmanaged shadow IT accounts and integrating disparate AWS accounts under centralized organization control to enforce consistent security baselines.
